257	  refused, and the file is left untouched.
258	- ✅ After a failed or partial write, the handle refuses all further appends, so nothing gets
259	  written out of line with the 48-byte slots. Tested by lowering `RLIMIT_FSIZE` to make a real
260	  `write()` fail.
261	- ✅ The fd is `O_CLOEXEC`, so it isn't inherited across `exec` by supervised children.
262	- ❌ **No `fsync` yet.** A power cut can lose records the kernel hasn't written to the card yet.
263	- ❌ **No recovery yet.** If a crash leaves a partial record at the end, reopening appends after
264	  it, out of line. The recovery step fixes this.
265	- ❌ One writer per file is assumed. The design gives storage a single writer process (`stored`).
266	- Open question for recovery: a file of 1–23 bytes is refused today. It could be a crash during
267	  header creation (ours) or a stranger's file, and there's no way to tell them apart.
268	
269	**Remaining storage steps:** (4) recovery: scan, validate each CRC, truncate at the first bad
270	record, report what was discarded; (5) write batching + `fsync` policy, with counters for the
271	fsync experiment. After those: segment rotation, `MANIFEST`, nightly rollups, free-space guard,
272	the `dsq` query CLI.
273	
274	### Building and running on the Pi
275	
276	- From a Mac or Linux clone: `make deploy PI=<user>@<host>` (rsync; copies changed files, skips
277	  `.git`, `build`, `transcripts`), then on the Pi `cd ~/term-project && make test && make memcheck`.
278	- `valgrind` only runs on Linux. The Pi or a CS department machine is where `make memcheck` means
279	  something.
280	- **Linux-only code needs a Makefile split that doesn't exist yet.** The Makefile currently builds
281	  every file in `SRC` on every machine, and one partner develops on macOS. Code that includes
282	  `<linux/i2c-dev.h>` or calls `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` would break the Mac build if it went straight
283	  into `SRC`. Keeping it in `src/sensors/` (per `CLAUDE.md`) and adding it through a Linux-only
284	  variable (e.g. `ifeq ($(shell uname -s),Linux)`) keeps `make test` working everywhere.
285	
286	### Open work for M2 (none of it is started)
287	
288	**1. `DESIGN.md`** (10 pts, team). Spec §8: architecture with rates on every arrow, mechanism
289	mapping justified from the user's requirements, failure-mode table, storage and data,
290	constraints and substitutions, evaluation plan, ownership map, AI-use plan. Sources:
291	`design-review.md` §5 (architecture), §8–9 (data, storage), §10–11 (processes, IPC), §12
292	(failure modes), §13 (evaluation).
293	
294	**2. Sensors electrically alive.** Evidence goes in `hardware-log.md` §1–5: `i2cdetect -y 1`
295	should show `0x29`, `0x5A`, `0x76`/`0x77`. BME280 chip ID first, since it has a return window.
296	
297	**3. Sensor-reading code, `src/sensors/`** (the CLAUDE.md ownership map lists this area under
298	mechanism E). Nothing exists. A natural split that can be built and tested without hardware:
299	
300	- **Pure conversion functions:** register bytes in, fixed-point units out (the proposed payload
301	  above). No I/O, so they build anywhere. Unit-test them with the worked examples in the
302	  datasheets.
303	- **A thin Linux I2C layer:** `open("/dev/i2c-1")` + `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` with a combined
304	  write-then-read (repeated start). Linux-only, see the Makefile note above.
305	- **A one-shot check program** that reads all three sensors once and prints values. This is the
306	  M2 "electrically alive" evidence, and it becomes the core of `skyd` / `cloudd` / `envd` at M3.
307	
308	**Register facts to start from. Verify every one against the datasheet PDF before relying on
309	it. The team rule is evidence over recall, and these came from recall.**
310	
311	| Sensor | Address | Identity check | Key registers / protocol | Gotchas |
312	|---|---|---|---|---|
313	| BME280 | `0x76` (or `0x77`) | `0xD0` → `0x60`. `0x58` means a BMP280 (no humidity) | Calibration `0x88–0xA1` and `0xE1–0xE7`; `ctrl_hum 0xF2`, `ctrl_meas 0xF4`, `config 0xF5`; data burst `0xF7–0xFE` (P, T, H). Forced mode: write `ctrl_meas` with mode `01`, wait, read | Write `ctrl_hum` **before** `ctrl_meas` or the humidity setting is ignored. Use the datasheet's integer compensation code (32-bit T and H, 64-bit P); temperature must be computed first because P and H use its `t_fine` |
314	| TSL2591 | `0x29` | ID register `0x12` → `0x50` | Every register access goes through the command byte `0xA0 \| reg`. `ENABLE 0x00` (PON + AEN = `0x03`), `CONTROL 0x01` (gain bits 5:4, integration time bits 2:0: 100–600 ms), `STATUS 0x13` (AVALID bit 0), CH0 `0x14–0x15`, CH1 `0x16–0x17`, little-endian | At max gain indoors it saturates. The dark offset (hardware-log §5) is the noise floor every night reading sits on |
315	| MLX90614 | `0x5A` | — | SMBus read-word from RAM: `0x06` = ambient, `0x07` = object. Returns 3 bytes: LSB, MSB, PEC. `°C = raw × 0.02 − 273.15` | Needs a **repeated start** (combined write-read). PEC is CRC-8 (poly `0x07`) over addr+W, command, addr+R, LSB, MSB: check it. MSB bit 7 set on an object reading = error flag. Known Pi problem with this chip's clock stretching: lower `i2c_arm_baudrate` or use `i2c-gpio` (design-review §3) |
316	
317	**4. Supervisor + IPC (mechanism E)** — not needed for M2, needed for M3. `design-review.md`
318	§10–11: `dskyd` fork/execs the children, sees each death through pipe EOF / `SIGCHLD`, restarts with
319	exponential backoff, and gives up with a logged `DEAD` state on a restart storm. Can be built and
320	tested on any Linux machine with stand-in child processes; no sensors needed.
321	
322	**5. Process items for M2.** Each partner copies out their `.jsonl` transcripts to
323	`transcripts/<name>/<date>-m2/`. Each partner's `PROMPTLOG` needs, at some point, a review of
324	the *other* partner's code. `src/store/` and `src/common/` are reviewable now. The ownership map's
325	"proposed" side still needs confirming in `CLAUDE.md`.

1. **Hub → storage:** `AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET`, one record per message. `stored` accepts
   `fusiond` and `dskyd` and stays the only writer. While `stored` is down, `fusiond` buffers 4096

2. **Durability:** `write()` every 10 s or 64 records; `fsync()` every 60 s, at rotation and at
   shutdown; directory `fsync()` after creating a segment.
3. **Segments:** one per night, rotated at local noon (every 24 h of monotonic time when the clock
   is unsynced), 32 MB cap. No MANIFEST: recovery scans only the open segment.
4. **Retention:** raw 180 days, rollups forever; raw writes stop below 2 GB free.
5. **Torn header:** a 1–23-byte file with our segment name in our data directory is recreated; any
   other short file is still refused.
6. **`seq` per (source, run):** a new kind START (= 6) opens every run, carrying the run number
   from `dskyd`.
7. **Failures in records:** an I/O failure is a FAULT (the first, then ≤ 1 per 60 s); an
   implausible value is a SAMPLE without `VALID`.
8. **`source_id`s:** 0 reserved, 1 `skyd`, 2 `cloudd`, 3 `envd`, 4 `fusiond`, 5 `dskyd`,

9. **Payloads:** Nick's SAMPLE table adopted as is; FEATURE, STATE, HEARTBEAT, FAULT and START
   added; new flag `CLOCK_UNSYNC` = bit 4. No layout change. See `record-and-ipc.md`.
10. **Analysis split:** Liam takes the classifier + state machine; Nick takes features,
    ephemeris and `dsq`.
11. **Evaluation targets in Nick's area:** row 2 (durable p99 ≤ 61 s), 10 (`fsync` sweep, ≤ 30
    MB/day written at 60 s), 11 (power cut 20/20, ≤ 60 s lost), 12 (ephemeris ≤ 0.1° sun, ≤ 0.5°
    moon).

### Decided in Liam's area (mechanism E)

Three sensor daemons share the bus; an I2C broker is the fallback if p99 interval jitter > 100 ms.
Shared-memory single-producer/single-consumer rings, chosen for decoupled lifetimes. One thread
per process. A hang is detected after 20 s of a silent liveness pipe. A "sensor absent" exit code
→ `DEAD` + re-probe every 60 s. Crash backoff 1 → 60 s; 5 crashes in 300 s → `DEAD`. systemd

project with both partners well represented.

### Hardware

All parts arrived 2026-10-13. The Pi was set up headless on 2026-10-27. Full detail and raw output
are in [`hardware-log.md`](hardware-log.md) §0.

### Code that exists

Everything below builds with `-std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror` and passes `make test` and
`make asan` on macOS. Steps 0–2 also pass `make memcheck` on the Pi.

| File | What it is | Owner (CLAUDE.md map) |
|---|---|---|
| `Makefile` | One test binary `build/test_all`; targets `test`, `asan`, `memcheck`, `deploy`, `clean`, `help`. `-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L` is required for glibc to declare `fsync`, `pread`, `clock_gettime`, etc. under `-std=c17` | shared |
| `tests/check.h`, `tests/test_main.c`, `tests/suites.h` | `CHECK(cond, fmt, ...)` counts and prints failures; `main` runs every suite and exits non-zero on any failure | shared |
| `src/common/crc32.{c,h}` | `dsm_crc32(data, len)`: CRC-32/IEEE, bit-at-a-time. Tested against the published check value `0xCBF43926` | Nick |
| `src/common/record.{c,h}` | `struct dsm_record`: **the 48-byte format every process shares** (see the contract below) | Nick |
| `src/store/store.{c,h}` | Append-only store file: a 24-byte header, then records back to back | Nick |

Tests: 116 checks across `tests/test_crc32.c`, `tests/test_record.c`, `tests/test_store.c`.

### The record contract (`src/common/record.h`)

Everything that produces data produces `struct dsm_record`. The rules:

1. `record_init(&r, kind, source_id)` first. It zeroes all 48 bytes. Uninitialized bytes would be
   fed into the CRC, which valgrind reports.
2. Fill in the fields.
3. `record_seal(&r)` **last**. Any change after sealing makes `record_intact()` false.
4. `seq` counts per source, starting at 0, +1 per record. A gap is provable lost data.
5. `t_mono_ns` = `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (for intervals); `t_real_ns` = `CLOCK_REALTIME` (wall-clock
   label).
6. Replayed or simulated data **must** set `DSM_FLAG_SYNTHETIC` (spec §5).
7. Values in `v[0..3]` are integers (fixed-point), never floats.

**The store refuses any record that isn't sealed** (`STORE_ERR_BADREC`). That's deliberate. Crash
recovery will cut a file off at its first bad record, so letting one unsealed record in would cost
every good record written after it.

### Proposed sample payload (NOT agreed — both partners to decide)

Which `source_id` each sensor uses, and what goes in each `v[]` slot, is a cross-boundary
interface. Nothing depends on it yet. This is only a starting proposal:

| `source_id` | Process / sensor | `v[0]` | `v[1]` | `v[2]` | `v[3]` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | *(reserved: a zeroed record must never look real)* | | | | |
| 1 | `skyd` / TSL2591 | CH0 raw count (full spectrum) | CH1 raw count (IR) | gain multiplier (1, 25, 428, 9876) | integration time, ms |
| 2 | `cloudd` / MLX90614 | sky (object) temp, m°C | sensor (ambient) temp, m°C | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | `envd` / BME280 | temperature, m°C | humidity, milli-%RH | pressure, Pa | 0 |

The reasoning behind it:

- **Raw TSL2591 counts rather than lux.** Lux isn't meaningful at night-sky levels, and the
  design converts brightness to relative mag/arcsec² as a *feature* later (`design-review.md` §6).
  Storing raw counts plus gain and integration time means that conversion can be redone from old
  data.
- **The MLX90614 reports in steps of 0.02 K**, which is exactly 20 m°C, so milli-degrees store it
  with no rounding: `m°C = raw * 20 - 273150`.

Still open: how a failed read is recorded (a `FAULT` record, or a `SAMPLE` without
`DSM_FLAG_VALID`), and the `source_id`s for `fusiond` and the supervisor.

### Store API (`src/store/store.h`) as of today

```c
enum store_status store_open(const char *path, struct dsm_store **out);   /* create or reopen */
enum store_status store_append(struct dsm_store *s, const struct dsm_record *r);
enum store_status store_close(struct dsm_store *s);                         /* NULL-safe */
```

Status values: `STORE_OK`, `STORE_ERR_IO` (check `errno`), `STORE_ERR_FORMAT` (an existing file
that isn't ours; refused, left untouched), `STORE_ERR_BADREC` (unsealed record; nothing written),
`STORE_ERR_BROKEN` (an earlier write failed; no more appends on this handle).

What it guarantees **today**, and what it doesn't:

- ✅ New file gets a header: magic `DSKY`, schema version, record size, creation time, CRC.
  Reopening appends at the end and never rewrites the header.
- ✅ Wrong magic, schema, or record size, a damaged header, or a file shorter than a header →
  refused, and the file is left untouched.
- ✅ After a failed or partial write, the handle refuses all further appends, so nothing gets
  written out of line with the 48-byte slots. Tested by lowering `RLIMIT_FSIZE` to make a real
  `write()` fail.
- ✅ The fd is `O_CLOEXEC`, so it isn't inherited across `exec` by supervised children.
- ❌ **No `fsync` yet.** A power cut can lose records the kernel hasn't written to the card yet.
- ❌ **No recovery yet.** If a crash leaves a partial record at the end, reopening appends after
  it, out of line. The recovery step fixes this.
- ❌ One writer per file is assumed. The design gives storage a single writer process (`stored`).
- Open question for recovery: a file of 1–23 bytes is refused today. It could be a crash during
  header creation (ours) or a stranger's file, and there's no way to tell them apart.

**Remaining storage steps:** (4) recovery: scan, validate each CRC, truncate at the first bad
record, report what was discarded; (5) write batching + `fsync` policy, with counters for the
fsync experiment. After those: segment rotation, `MANIFEST`, nightly rollups, free-space guard,
the `dsq` query CLI.

### Building and running on the Pi

- From a Mac or Linux clone: `make deploy PI=<user>@<host>` (rsync; copies changed files, skips
  `.git`, `build`, `transcripts`), then on the Pi `cd ~/term-project && make test && make memcheck`.
- `valgrind` only runs on Linux. The Pi or a CS department machine is where `make memcheck` means
  something.
- **Linux-only code needs a Makefile split that doesn't exist yet.** The Makefile currently builds
  every file in `SRC` on every machine, and one partner develops on macOS. Code that includes
  `<linux/i2c-dev.h>` or calls `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` would break the Mac build if it went straight
  into `SRC`. Keeping it in `src/sensors/` (per `CLAUDE.md`) and adding it through a Linux-only
  variable (e.g. `ifeq ($(shell uname -s),Linux)`) keeps `make test` working everywhere.

### Open work for M2 (none of it is started)

**1. `DESIGN.md`** (10 pts, team). Spec §8: architecture with rates on every arrow, mechanism
mapping justified from the user's requirements, failure-mode table, storage and data,
constraints and substitutions, evaluation plan, ownership map, AI-use plan. Sources:
`design-review.md` §5 (architecture), §8–9 (data, storage), §10–11 (processes, IPC), §12
(failure modes), §13 (evaluation).

**2. Sensors electrically alive.** Evidence goes in `hardware-log.md` §1–5: `i2cdetect -y 1`
should show `0x29`, `0x5A`, `0x76`/`0x77`. BME280 chip ID first, since it has a return window.

**3. Sensor-reading code, `src/sensors/`** (the CLAUDE.md ownership map lists this area under
mechanism E). Nothing exists. A natural split that can be built and tested without hardware:

- **Pure conversion functions:** register bytes in, fixed-point units out (the proposed payload
  above). No I/O, so they build anywhere. Unit-test them with the worked examples in the
  datasheets.
- **A thin Linux I2C layer:** `open("/dev/i2c-1")` + `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` with a combined
  write-then-read (repeated start). Linux-only, see the Makefile note above.
- **A one-shot check program** that reads all three sensors once and prints values. This is the
  M2 "electrically alive" evidence, and it becomes the core of `skyd` / `cloudd` / `envd` at M3.

**Register facts to start from. Verify every one against the datasheet PDF before relying on
it. The team rule is evidence over recall, and these came from recall.**

| Sensor | Address | Identity check | Key registers / protocol | Gotchas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BME280 | `0x76` (or `0x77`) | `0xD0` → `0x60`. `0x58` means a BMP280 (no humidity) | Calibration `0x88–0xA1` and `0xE1–0xE7`; `ctrl_hum 0xF2`, `ctrl_meas 0xF4`, `config 0xF5`; data burst `0xF7–0xFE` (P, T, H). Forced mode: write `ctrl_meas` with mode `01`, wait, read | Write `ctrl_hum` **before** `ctrl_meas` or the humidity setting is ignored. Use the datasheet's integer compensation code (32-bit T and H, 64-bit P); temperature must be computed first because P and H use its `t_fine` |
| TSL2591 | `0x29` | ID register `0x12` → `0x50` | Every register access goes through the command byte `0xA0 \| reg`. `ENABLE 0x00` (PON + AEN = `0x03`), `CONTROL 0x01` (gain bits 5:4, integration time bits 2:0: 100–600 ms), `STATUS 0x13` (AVALID bit 0), CH0 `0x14–0x15`, CH1 `0x16–0x17`, little-endian | At max gain indoors it saturates. The dark offset (hardware-log §5) is the noise floor every night reading sits on |
| MLX90614 | `0x5A` | — | SMBus read-word from RAM: `0x06` = ambient, `0x07` = object. Returns 3 bytes: LSB, MSB, PEC. `°C = raw × 0.02 − 273.15` | Needs a **repeated start** (combined write-read). PEC is CRC-8 (poly `0x07`) over addr+W, command, addr+R, LSB, MSB: check it. MSB bit 7 set on an object reading = error flag. Known Pi problem with this chip's clock stretching: lower `i2c_arm_baudrate` or use `i2c-gpio` (design-review §3) |

**4. Supervisor + IPC (mechanism E)** — not needed for M2, needed for M3. `design-review.md`
§10–11: `dskyd` fork/execs the children, sees each death through pipe EOF / `SIGCHLD`, restarts with
exponential backoff, and gives up with a logged `DEAD` state on a restart storm. Can be built and
tested on any Linux machine with stand-in child processes; no sensors needed.

**5. Process items for M2.** Each partner copies out their `.jsonl` transcripts to
`transcripts/<name>/<date>-m2/`. Each partner's `PROMPTLOG` needs, at some point, a review of
the *other* partner's code. `src/store/` and `src/common/` are reviewable now. The ownership map's

37	Every channel is `AF_UNIX`, a pipe, shm or a signal: **no IP sockets**. **Supervision:** `dskyd`
38	(under systemd) fork/execs the five children, watches a per-child liveness pipe (EOF = died, 20 s
39	silent = hung → `SIGKILL`), restarts with 1→60 s backoff, parks an absent sensor as `DEAD` with a
40	60 s re-probe, and logs hourly HEARTBEATs; stderr → journald. Rates and channel details:
41	[`docs/record-and-ipc.md`](docs/record-and-ipc.md).

43	## Mechanism mapping
44	
45	Each GOOD acted on costs the user **30–45 min of setup or a 30–60 min drive**; the product's value
46	is a **site baseline built over weeks** (PROBLEM.md).
47	
48	**E: multi-process + IPC + supervisor** (`dskyd`, one process per sensor, `fusiond`; shm rings,
49	`AF_UNIX` sockets). **R-E1:** a dead, hung or unplugged sensor turns the verdict UNKNOWN within
50	**60 s** while the others keep sampling. **R-E2:** a crash costs ≤ **10 s** of that sensor's
51	data. *Why:* at a dark site, overcast reads *darker* than clear, so a silent IR sensor yields a
52	confident false GOOD, the error that wastes the evening. In one process, one hung `ioctl` stalls
53	every sensor; separate processes keep failures local, `fusiond` flags staleness after 3 missed
54	periods (≤ 30 s), and analysis restarts without stopping sampling.
55	
56	**D: crash-consistent storage** (`stored`, record format). **R-D1:** a power cut loses
57	≤ **60 s** of records, never an earlier one. **R-D2:** automatic recovery, **20/20** pulled-plug
58	tests. **R-D3:** ≥ **180 days** raw plus all rollups fit the 16 GB card. *Why:* the baseline *is*
59	the product's memory, and a yard extension cord sees brownouts (spec §17). Verdicts use 30-min
60	windows, so losing ≤ 60 s (≤ 3 %) can't flip a night: hence `fsync` every 60 s, with 10 s write
61	batching to spare the card; CRC-sealed fixed-size records make truncation a complete recovery.
62

64	speed**. Publish-after-write (release/acquire on `head`), CRC check on read, never overwrite
65	unread (`head − tail < N`), reader-restart duplicates removed by (source, run, seq), lock-free
66	`_Static_assert` (**assumed, confirmed at build on the Pi**). **Rejected:** C, F (nothing at 1.3
67	rec/s has a deadline or rate to sustain); A is a stretch; B needs a pulse-output sensor.

1	# Record format, data rates, and IPC
2	
3	Detail behind `DESIGN.md` § Architecture, § Mechanism mapping and § Storage and data. The record
4	and header layouts are **implemented** (`src/common/record.h`, `src/store/store.h`). Everything
5	marked *proposed* in the record sections (the kinds, flags, `source_id`s and payloads, which
6	nothing depends on yet) was proposed by Liam and **confirmed by Nick on 2026-10-28**. The IPC section is Liam's
7	(mechanism E). The IPC is designed but not implemented.
8	
9	## Record: 48 bytes, little-endian (implemented)
10	
11	| Offset | Size | Field | Meaning |
12	|---|---|---|---|
13	| 0 | 8 | `t_mono_ns` | `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, for intervals |
14	| 8 | 8 | `t_real_ns` | `CLOCK_REALTIME`, the wall-clock label |
15	| 16 | 2 | `schema_ver` | `DSM_SCHEMA_VER` (1) |
16	| 18 | 2 | `source_id` | producing process (table below) |
17	| 20 | 2 | `kind` | record kind (table below) |
18	| 22 | 2 | `flags` | bit flags (table below) |
19	| 24 | 16 | `v[4]` | `int32` fixed-point values; meaning depends on `source_id` and `kind` |
20	| 40 | 4 | `seq` | per (source, run) counter |
21	| 44 | 4 | `crc32` | CRC-32/IEEE over bytes 0–43 |
22	
23	The layout is enforced at compile time with `_Static_assert`. Rules: `record_init()` zeroes all
24	48 bytes first; `record_seal()` is called last; the store refuses unsealed records.
25	
26	## Segment header: 24 bytes (implemented)
27	
28	`magic "DSKY"` (4) · `schema_ver` (2) · `record_size` (2) · `created_real_ns` (8) · `reserved`
29	(4, always 0) · `crc32` over bytes 0–19 (4). On reopen, any mismatch means the file is refused
30	and left untouched.
31	
32	## Kinds and flags
33	
34	| `kind` | Value | | Flag | Bit |
35	|---|---|---|---|---|
36	| SAMPLE | 1 | | `VALID` | 0 |
37	| FEATURE | 2 | | `STALE` | 1 |
38	| STATE | 3 | | `SYNTHETIC` (all replayed or provoked data) | 2 |
39	| HEARTBEAT | 4 | | `CALIBRATING` (sensor warming up) | 3 |
40	| FAULT | 5 | | `CLOCK_UNSYNC` (*proposed*) | 4 |
41	| START (*proposed*) | 6 | | | |
42	
43	0 is never a valid kind or `source_id`, so a zeroed record never looks real.
44	
45	## Payloads (proposed)
46	
47	| `source_id` | `kind` | `v[0]` | `v[1]` | `v[2]` | `v[3]` |
48	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
49	| 1 `skyd` | SAMPLE | TSL2591 CH0 count (full spectrum) | CH1 count (IR) | gain multiplier | integration, ms |
50	| 2 `cloudd` | SAMPLE | sky (object) temp, m°C | ambient (die) temp, m°C | 0 | 0 |
51	| 3 `envd` | SAMPLE | temperature, m°C | humidity, milli-%RH | pressure, Pa | 0 |
52	| 4 `fusiond` | FEATURE | feature id | value ×1000 | window, s | samples in window |
53	| 4 `fusiond` | STATE | state | rules fired (bitmask) | confidence ×1000 | 0 |
54	| 5 `dskyd` | HEARTBEAT | subject `source_id` | RSS, KiB | CPU time, ms | cumulative events |
55	| any (6 = `stored`) | FAULT | fault code | errno | consecutive count | 0 |
56	| any | START | run number (from `dskyd`) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
57	
58	- **Raw counts, not lux,** for the TSL2591: lux means little at night-sky levels, and storing
59	  counts plus gain and integration time lets the brightness conversion be redone later.
60	- **MLX90614 in m°C:** its 0.02 K step is exactly 20 m°C (`m°C = raw × 20 − 273150`), so there
61	  is no rounding (datasheet scale, verify at bring-up).
62	- **FAULT vs. `!VALID`:** an I/O failure is a FAULT (the first one, then at most 1 per 60 s while
63	  it lasts); a successful read with an implausible value (saturated, MLX error bit) is a SAMPLE
64	  with `VALID` cleared.
65	- **`seq` per run:** each process start writes START with `seq` 0. A gap within a run is
66	  provable loss; the time between runs is the restart gap.
67	
68	## Rate derivation (computed, not measured)
69	
70	| Record | Rate | Records/day |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| `skyd` SAMPLE | 1 per 5 s | 17 280 |
73	| `cloudd` SAMPLE | 1 per 1 s | 86 400 |
74	| `envd` SAMPLE | 1 per 10 s | 8 640 |
75	| FEATURE | 4 per min | 5 760 |
76	| STATE | on change, ≥ 1 per 10 min | ≥ 144 |
77	| HEARTBEAT | 6 per h (5 children + `dskyd`) | 144 |
78	| FAULT, START | per event | ≈ 0 in steady state |
79	| **Total** | **≈ 1.37 rec/s** | **≈ 118 400 → 5.7 MB/day** |
80	
81	- 180 days of raw data ≈ 1.0 GB, on a 16 GB card.
82	- `write()` every 10 s ≈ 13.7 records ≈ 660 B per call; `fsync()` 1440 per day.
83	- I2C transfers (planned read sequences; datasheet protocol, verify at bring-up): TSL2591 status
84	  + data = 2 per sample → 0.4/s; MLX90614 ambient + object = 2 → 2/s; BME280 trigger + burst = 2
85	  → 0.2/s. **≈ 2.6 transfers/s in total.**
86	- Buffer headroom: a 1024-slot ring holds 17 min of `cloudd`, 85 min of `skyd` and 170 min of
87	  `envd`; `fusiond`'s 4096-record buffer for `stored` holds ≈ 50 min.
88	
89	## IPC (mechanism E)
90	
91	### Sensor → `fusiond`: shared-memory rings
92	
93	One single-producer/single-consumer ring per sensor daemon: 1024 slots × 48 B in POSIX shared
94	memory under `/dev/shm`, plus one shared semaphore that every producer posts and `fusiond` waits
95	on with a 1 s timeout. `dskyd` creates the shared memory before the fork and unlinks it on
96	orderly shutdown, so a ring outlives the restart of either side.
97	
98	Chosen over sockets for **decoupled lifetimes, not speed** (1.3 rec/s is slow): samples keep
99	queuing while `fusiond` restarts, and a sensor never blocks on the hub.
100	
101	**Invariants:**
102	
103	1. **Publish after write:** fill slot `head % N` with an already-sealed record, *then* advance
104	   `head` with a release store. The reader acquire-loads `head` and reads only slots below it, so
105	   a producer `kill -9`'d mid-copy never exposes a half-written slot. The restarted producer
106	   reads `head` from shared memory and overwrites that same slot.
107	2. **CRC on read:** the reader copies the slot out and checks `record_intact()` before use. A
108	   torn slot (a bug, not the protocol) is counted and dropped, never trusted.
109	3. **Never overwrite unread:** the producer writes only while `head − tail < N`. When the ring is
110	   full, it drops the *new* sample and increments an overrun counter in the ring header; the
111	   `seq` gap proves the loss.
112	4. **Reader restart:** `tail` advances only after the record has been forwarded to `stored`. If
113	   `fusiond` is killed in between, the restarted `fusiond` re-sends that record. The duplicate
114	   has the same (source, run, seq) and is removed at query time.
115	5. **Lock-free across processes:** `_Static_assert(ATOMIC_INT_LOCK_FREE == 2)`, because a
116	   lock-based atomic would deadlock if a process died holding the lock. **Assumed, confirmed at
117	   build on the Pi** (64-bit ARM).
118	
119	Edge cases: a producer killed between advancing `head` and posting the semaphore only delays
120	the record until the reader's next 1 s timeout.
121	
122	### Other channels
123	
124	| Channel | Kernel object | Rate | Notes |
125	|---|---|---|---|
126	| `fusiond` → `stored`, `dskyd` → `stored` | `AF_UNIX` `SOCK_SEQPACKET`, one 48-byte record per message | 1.37 rec/s; 6 rec/h | `stored` is the only writer. While it is down, `fusiond` buffers 4096 records (≈ 50 min), then drops the oldest and counts. **Proposed (Liam), confirmed (Nick) 2026-10-28** |
127	| `dsq` ↔ `fusiond` | `AF_UNIX` `SOCK_STREAM`, line-based request/response | on demand | `state`, `health`. `dsq` reads segments directly, read-only |
128	| `dskyd` ↔ each child | pipe (child holds the write end) + `SIGCHLD` | ≥ 1 B per 5 s | EOF = died; 20 s silent = hung → `SIGKILL` |
129	| all → log | stderr → journald | ≈ 6 lines/h steady + 1 per event | survives a `dskyd` crash |
130	
131	### Supervision (`dskyd`)
132	
133	- Runs under systemd with `Restart=on-failure`; children set `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`, so they exit
134	  with it and a restarted `dskyd` starts a clean tree.
135	- After a crash: restart with 1 → 2 → 4 … 60 s backoff; 60 s of healthy running resets it.
136	- A sensor daemon that sees 3 consecutive failed reads exits with a distinct "sensor absent"
137	  code. `dskyd` marks it `DEAD` and re-probes every 60 s instead of restarting fast, so an
138	  unplugged sensor never causes a restart storm.
139	- 5 crashes within 300 s → `DEAD`, re-probe every 60 s; the rest of the system keeps running.
140	- Heartbeat: one HEARTBEAT per child within 60 s of start, then hourly. Contents: RSS and CPU
141	  time from `/proc/<pid>/statm` and `/stat`, plus cumulative events from the ring counters.
142	- Each child passes its run number in its START record (see `seq` above).

174	- Installed: `git build-essential i2c-tools valgrind rsync`. I2C is on (`/dev/i2c-1` exists).
175	- Power: `vcgencmd get_throttled` → `0x0`.
176	- First Linux build of the project: `make test` 15/0, `make memcheck` 0 errors, no leaks.
177	- **Not done yet:** sensor wiring, `i2cdetect`, BME280 chip ID, and the rest of the bring-up
178	  checklist in `hardware-log.md` §1–5.
179	- **No RTC** (DS3231 deferred). The Pi gets the real time from the network at boot. Without a
180	  network, `CLOCK_REALTIME` is wrong after a power cut, and so is anything that depends on it
181	  (`t_real_ns`, and later the sun/moon calculations).
182	
183	### Code that exists
184	
185	Everything below builds with `-std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror` and passes `make test` and
186	`make asan` on macOS. Steps 0–2 also pass `make memcheck` on the Pi.
187	
188	| File | What it is | Owner (CLAUDE.md map) |
189	|---|---|---|
190	| `Makefile` | One test binary `build/test_all`; targets `test`, `asan`, `memcheck`, `deploy`, `clean`, `help`. `-D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L` is required for glibc to declare `fsync`, `pread`, `clock_gettime`, etc. under `-std=c17` | shared |
191	| `tests/check.h`, `tests/test_main.c`, `tests/suites.h` | `CHECK(cond, fmt, ...)` counts and prints failures; `main` runs every suite and exits non-zero on any failure | shared |
192	| `src/common/crc32.{c,h}` | `dsm_crc32(data, len)`: CRC-32/IEEE, bit-at-a-time. Tested against the published check value `0xCBF43926` | Nick |
193	| `src/common/record.{c,h}` | `struct dsm_record`: **the 48-byte format every process shares** (see the contract below) | Nick |
194	| `src/store/store.{c,h}` | Append-only store file: a 24-byte header, then records back to back | Nick |
195	
196	Tests: 116 checks across `tests/test_crc32.c`, `tests/test_record.c`, `tests/test_store.c`.
197	
198	### The record contract (`src/common/record.h`)
199	
200	Everything that produces data produces `struct dsm_record`. The rules:
201	
202	1. `record_init(&r, kind, source_id)` first. It zeroes all 48 bytes. Uninitialized bytes would be
203	   fed into the CRC, which valgrind reports.
204	2. Fill in the fields.
205	3. `record_seal(&r)` **last**. Any change after sealing makes `record_intact()` false.
206	4. `seq` counts per source, starting at 0, +1 per record. A gap is provable lost data.
207	5. `t_mono_ns` = `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (for intervals); `t_real_ns` = `CLOCK_REALTIME` (wall-clock
208	   label).
209	6. Replayed or simulated data **must** set `DSM_FLAG_SYNTHETIC` (spec §5).
210	7. Values in `v[0..3]` are integers (fixed-point), never floats.
211	
212	**The store refuses any record that isn't sealed** (`STORE_ERR_BADREC`). That's deliberate. Crash
213	recovery will cut a file off at its first bad record, so letting one unsealed record in would cost
214	every good record written after it.
215	
216	### Proposed sample payload (NOT agreed — both partners to decide)
217	
218	Which `source_id` each sensor uses, and what goes in each `v[]` slot, is a cross-boundary
219	interface. Nothing depends on it yet. This is only a starting proposal:
220	
221	| `source_id` | Process / sensor | `v[0]` | `v[1]` | `v[2]` | `v[3]` |
222	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
223	| 0 | *(reserved: a zeroed record must never look real)* | | | | |
224	| 1 | `skyd` / TSL2591 | CH0 raw count (full spectrum) | CH1 raw count (IR) | gain multiplier (1, 25, 428, 9876) | integration time, ms |
225	| 2 | `cloudd` / MLX90614 | sky (object) temp, m°C | sensor (ambient) temp, m°C | 0 | 0 |
226	| 3 | `envd` / BME280 | temperature, m°C | humidity, milli-%RH | pressure, Pa | 0 |
227	
228	The reasoning behind it:
229	
230	- **Raw TSL2591 counts rather than lux.** Lux isn't meaningful at night-sky levels, and the
231	  design converts brightness to relative mag/arcsec² as a *feature* later (`design-review.md` §6).
232	  Storing raw counts plus gain and integration time means that conversion can be redone from old
233	  data.
234	- **The MLX90614 reports in steps of 0.02 K**, which is exactly 20 m°C, so milli-degrees store it
235	  with no rounding: `m°C = raw * 20 - 273150`.
236	
237	Still open: how a failed read is recorded (a `FAULT` record, or a `SAMPLE` without
238	`DSM_FLAG_VALID`), and the `source_id`s for `fusiond` and the supervisor.
239	
240	### Store API (`src/store/store.h`) as of today
241	
242	```c
243	enum store_status store_open(const char *path, struct dsm_store **out);   /* create or reopen */
244	enum store_status store_append(struct dsm_store *s, const struct dsm_record *r);
245	enum store_status store_close(struct dsm_store *s);                         /* NULL-safe */
246	```
247	
248	Status values: `STORE_OK`, `STORE_ERR_IO` (check `errno`), `STORE_ERR_FORMAT` (an existing file
249	that isn't ours; refused, left untouched), `STORE_ERR_BADREC` (unsealed record; nothing written),
250	`STORE_ERR_BROKEN` (an earlier write failed; no more appends on this handle).
251	
252	What it guarantees **today**, and what it doesn't:
253	
254	- ✅ New file gets a header: magic `DSKY`, schema version, record size, creation time, CRC.
255	  Reopening appends at the end and never rewrites the header.
256	- ✅ Wrong magic, schema, or record size, a damaged header, or a file shorter than a header →
257	  refused, and the file is left untouched.
258	- ✅ After a failed or partial write, the handle refuses all further appends, so nothing gets
259	  written out of line with the 48-byte slots. Tested by lowering `RLIMIT_FSIZE` to make a real
260	  `write()` fail.
261	- ✅ The fd is `O_CLOEXEC`, so it isn't inherited across `exec` by supervised children.
262	- ❌ **No `fsync` yet.** A power cut can lose records the kernel hasn't written to the card yet.
263	- ❌ **No recovery yet.** If a crash leaves a partial record at the end, reopening appends after
264	  it, out of line. The recovery step fixes this.
265	- ❌ One writer per file is assumed. The design gives storage a single writer process (`stored`).
266	- Open question for recovery: a file of 1–23 bytes is refused today. It could be a crash during
267	  header creation (ours) or a stranger's file, and there's no way to tell them apart.
268	
269	**Remaining storage steps:** (4) recovery: scan, validate each CRC, truncate at the first bad
270	record, report what was discarded; (5) write batching + `fsync` policy, with counters for the
271	fsync experiment. After those: segment rotation, `MANIFEST`, nightly rollups, free-space guard,
272	the `dsq` query CLI.
273	
274	### Building and running on the Pi
275	
276	- From a Mac or Linux clone: `make deploy PI=<user>@<host>` (rsync; copies changed files, skips
277	  `.git`, `build`, `transcripts`), then on the Pi `cd ~/term-project && make test && make memcheck`.
278	- `valgrind` only runs on Linux. The Pi or a CS department machine is where `make memcheck` means
279	  something.
280	- **Linux-only code needs a Makefile split that doesn't exist yet.** The Makefile currently builds
281	  every file in `SRC` on every machine, and one partner develops on macOS. Code that includes
282	  `<linux/i2c-dev.h>` or calls `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` would break the Mac build if it went straight
283	  into `SRC`. Keeping it in `src/sensors/` (per `CLAUDE.md`) and adding it through a Linux-only
284	  variable (e.g. `ifeq ($(shell uname -s),Linux)`) keeps `make test` working everywhere.
285	
286	### Open work for M2 (none of it is started)
287	
288	**1. `DESIGN.md`** (10 pts, team). Spec §8: architecture with rates on every arrow, mechanism
289	mapping justified from the user's requirements, failure-mode table, storage and data,
290	constraints and substitutions, evaluation plan, ownership map, AI-use plan. Sources:
291	`design-review.md` §5 (architecture), §8–9 (data, storage), §10–11 (processes, IPC), §12
292	(failure modes), §13 (evaluation).
293	
294	**2. Sensors electrically alive.** Evidence goes in `hardware-log.md` §1–5: `i2cdetect -y 1`
295	should show `0x29`, `0x5A`, `0x76`/`0x77`. BME280 chip ID first, since it has a return window.
296	
297	**3. Sensor-reading code, `src/sensors/`** (the CLAUDE.md ownership map lists this area under
298	mechanism E). Nothing exists. A natural split that can be built and tested without hardware:
299	
300	- **Pure conversion functions:** register bytes in, fixed-point units out (the proposed payload
301	  above). No I/O, so they build anywhere. Unit-test them with the worked examples in the
302	  datasheets.
303	- **A thin Linux I2C layer:** `open("/dev/i2c-1")` + `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` with a combined
304	  write-then-read (repeated start). Linux-only, see the Makefile note above.
305	- **A one-shot check program** that reads all three sensors once and prints values. This is the
306	  M2 "electrically alive" evidence, and it becomes the core of `skyd` / `cloudd` / `envd` at M3.
307	
308	**Register facts to start from. Verify every one against the datasheet PDF before relying on
309	it. The team rule is evidence over recall, and these came from recall.**
310	
311	| Sensor | Address | Identity check | Key registers / protocol | Gotchas |
312	|---|---|---|---|---|
313	| BME280 | `0x76` (or `0x77`) | `0xD0` → `0x60`. `0x58` means a BMP280 (no humidity) | Calibration `0x88–0xA1` and `0xE1–0xE7`; `ctrl_hum 0xF2`, `ctrl_meas 0xF4`, `config 0xF5`; data burst `0xF7–0xFE` (P, T, H). Forced mode: write `ctrl_meas` with mode `01`, wait, read | Write `ctrl_hum` **before** `ctrl_meas` or the humidity setting is ignored. Use the datasheet's integer compensation code (32-bit T and H, 64-bit P); temperature must be computed first because P and H use its `t_fine` |
314	| TSL2591 | `0x29` | ID register `0x12` → `0x50` | Every register access goes through the command byte `0xA0 \| reg`. `ENABLE 0x00` (PON + AEN = `0x03`), `CONTROL 0x01` (gain bits 5:4, integration time bits 2:0: 100–600 ms), `STATUS 0x13` (AVALID bit 0), CH0 `0x14–0x15`, CH1 `0x16–0x17`, little-endian | At max gain indoors it saturates. The dark offset (hardware-log §5) is the noise floor every night reading sits on |
315	| MLX90614 | `0x5A` | — | SMBus read-word from RAM: `0x06` = ambient, `0x07` = object. Returns 3 bytes: LSB, MSB, PEC. `°C = raw × 0.02 − 273.15` | Needs a **repeated start** (combined write-read). PEC is CRC-8 (poly `0x07`) over addr+W, command, addr+R, LSB, MSB: check it. MSB bit 7 set on an object reading = error flag. Known Pi problem with this chip's clock stretching: lower `i2c_arm_baudrate` or use `i2c-gpio` (design-review §3) |
316	
317	**4. Supervisor + IPC (mechanism E)** — not needed for M2, needed for M3. `design-review.md`
318	§10–11: `dskyd` fork/execs the children, sees each death through pipe EOF / `SIGCHLD`, restarts with
319	exponential backoff, and gives up with a logged `DEAD` state on a restart storm. Can be built and
320	tested on any Linux machine with stand-in child processes; no sensors needed.
321	
322	**5. Process items for M2.** Each partner copies out their `.jsonl` transcripts to
323	`transcripts/<name>/<date>-m2/`. Each partner's `PROMPTLOG` needs, at some point, a review of
324	the *other* partner's code. `src/store/` and `src/common/` are reviewable now. The ownership map's
325	"proposed" side still needs confirming in `CLAUDE.md`.

Mapped to the spec's milestones. Estimated dates assume Week 1 = Aug 24 — verify on Canvas.

| Week | Milestone | Work |
|---|---|---|
| **5** (now) | **M1** | **Contact the astronomy club/faculty. Order hardware today.** Write the memo. Copy transcripts. |
| **6** | | Sensors electrically alive. Raw logging to a flat file. **Start the observation logbook — every clear night from here is data you cannot get back.** |
| **7** | **M2** | Design document. Argue the architecture in ink. Decide: 3 processes vs. i2c broker; fsync policy; record format frozen. |
| **8** | | Storage layer: segments, CRC, recovery. First power-cut tests. Start overnight runs *now*, at small scale. |
| **9** | | Supervisor + IPC. `kill -9` survival. Ephemeris module + unit tests against almanac. |
| **10** | **M3** | **Checkpoint:** all three sensors through the real pipeline into real storage; D and E working. |
| **11** | | Feature extraction, humidity correction fitted from real data, replay harness. |
| **12** | | Veto classifier + state machine + hysteresis. Query CLI. Reference-SQM calibration night. |
| **13** | | Experiments: fsync sweep, recovery rate, kill-9 stats, I2C contention, confusion matrix, reliability diagram. |
| **14** | **M4** | Feature freeze. **48-h soak #1.** Fix what it finds. Soak #2. |
| **15** | **M5** | Evaluation report, DESIGN.md changelog, PROMPTLOG, REFLECTION, final transcripts. |
| **15–16** | **M6** | Demo day. |

### The single most important scheduling point

**The observation logbook starts in week 6, not week 11.** Clear nights in Fort Collins during
October and November are finite and unrecoverable. Every night you log while the code is still ugly
is a night you do not have to beg the weather for in week 13. The code can be rebuilt; the nights
cannot.

---

## 17. MVP definition (must be true at M3, week 10)

1. Three sensors sampling at their own rates through three supervised processes.
2. Records reaching the custom storage layer with CRCs and sequence numbers.
3. Supervisor survives `kill -9` of any child and logs it.
4. Storage recovers cleanly from a mid-write power cut.
5. A CLI that prints current state and dumps a time range.
6. Sun/moon ephemeris correct against almanac values.
7. A state machine emitting GOOD/MARGINAL/POOR/UNKNOWN with reason strings — even with rough
   thresholds. Tuning comes later; the *pipeline* must be real.

Anything beyond this is stretch. Ship the MVP early and spend weeks 11–13 on the analysis and the
measurements, which is where the points actually are.

## 18. Stretch goals (in priority order)

1. **Dew heater control loop** — resistor + MOSFET on the IR aperture, driven by `dewpoint_margin`.
   Turns a failure mode into a feature and adds a measurable control loop.
2. **Character driver (mechanism A)** — expose one sensor via `/dev`. Best resume line available.
   Keep the userspace path as a fallback and only start this if M3 is early.
3. **Condensation self-diagnosis** (failure mode 4) — clever, and a great defense question.
4. **Reference-SQM calibration** → absolute mag/arcsec² instead of relative.
5. **LAN dashboard** — last, and deliberately last. Spec §4.6 is blunt that interface ambition is
   where teams bleed time; a crisp CLI is more defensible and far more extensible at the
   live-modification station on demo day.

## 19. Biggest implementation risks

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **MLX90614 cannot see through plastic.** Acrylic and most plastics are opaque in the 8–14 µm band it uses. A sealed clear window **blinds the cloud sensor.** | **Project-threatening** | Open aperture under a rain hood, tilted ~15° for drainage; **or** a thin LDPE film window (polyethylene is reasonably LWIR-transparent — a bag or cling film, calibrated in place, replaced periodically). Test this in **week 6**, not week 12. |
| **MLX90614 I2C is finicky on the Pi** (SMBus / repeated-start behaviour) | High | Budget real time. Common fixes: lower the bus baudrate (`dtparam=i2c_arm_baudrate=50000`), or use the `i2c-gpio` bitbang overlay on separate pins. Get it reading in week 6 or reconsider the sensor. |
| **Weather refuses to cooperate.** Too few clear nights for a meaningful matrix | High | Log from week 6. Observation-level not night-level labels. Provoked conditions + replay harness. Narrow the claim (§14). |
| **TSL2591 at the bottom of its range.** Night sky is near its noise floor | Medium | Long integration times, dark-frame/offset characterisation in a sealed box, report *relative* brightness unless the SQM calibration happens. |
| **Humidity correction may not separate cleanly** | Medium | If regression on your own data fails to separate humid-clear from overcast, say so and narrow the cloud claim to dry conditions. That is a legitimate result. |

Mapped to the spec's milestones. Estimated dates assume Week 1 = Aug 24 — verify on Canvas.

| Week | Milestone | Work |
|---|---|---|
| **5** (now) | **M1** | **Contact the astronomy club/faculty. Order hardware today.** Write the memo. Copy transcripts. |
| **6** | | Sensors electrically alive. Raw logging to a flat file. **Start the observation logbook — every clear night from here is data you cannot get back.** |
| **7** | **M2** | Design document. Argue the architecture in ink. Decide: 3 processes vs. i2c broker; fsync policy; record format frozen. |
| **8** | | Storage layer: segments, CRC, recovery. First power-cut tests. Start overnight runs *now*, at small scale. |
| **9** | | Supervisor + IPC. `kill -9` survival. Ephemeris module + unit tests against almanac. |
| **10** | **M3** | **Checkpoint:** all three sensors through the real pipeline into real storage; D and E working. |
| **11** | | Feature extraction, humidity correction fitted from real data, replay harness. |
| **12** | | Veto classifier + state machine + hysteresis. Query CLI. Reference-SQM calibration night. |
| **13** | | Experiments: fsync sweep, recovery rate, kill-9 stats, I2C contention, confusion matrix, reliability diagram. |
| **14** | **M4** | Feature freeze. **48-h soak #1.** Fix what it finds. Soak #2. |
| **15** | **M5** | Evaluation report, DESIGN.md changelog, PROMPTLOG, REFLECTION, final transcripts. |
| **15–16** | **M6** | Demo day. |

### The single most important scheduling point

**The observation logbook starts in week 6, not week 11.** Clear nights in Fort Collins during
October and November are finite and unrecoverable. Every night you log while the code is still ugly
is a night you do not have to beg the weather for in week 13. The code can be rebuilt; the nights
cannot.

---

## 17. MVP definition (must be true at M3, week 10)

1. Three sensors sampling at their own rates through three supervised processes.
2. Records reaching the custom storage layer with CRCs and sequence numbers.
3. Supervisor survives `kill -9` of any child and logs it.
4. Storage recovers cleanly from a mid-write power cut.
5. A CLI that prints current state and dumps a time range.
6. Sun/moon ephemeris correct against almanac values.
7. A state machine emitting GOOD/MARGINAL/POOR/UNKNOWN with reason strings — even with rough
   thresholds. Tuning comes later; the *pipeline* must be real.

Anything beyond this is stretch. Ship the MVP early and spend weeks 11–13 on the analysis and the
measurements, which is where the points actually are.

## 18. Stretch goals (in priority order)

1. **Dew heater control loop** — resistor + MOSFET on the IR aperture, driven by `dewpoint_margin`.
   Turns a failure mode into a feature and adds a measurable control loop.
2. **Character driver (mechanism A)** — expose one sensor via `/dev`. Best resume line available.
   Keep the userspace path as a fallback and only start this if M3 is early.
3. **Condensation self-diagnosis** (failure mode 4) — clever, and a great defense question.
4. **Reference-SQM calibration** → absolute mag/arcsec² instead of relative.
5. **LAN dashboard** — last, and deliberately last. Spec §4.6 is blunt that interface ambition is
   where teams bleed time; a crisp CLI is more defensible and far more extensible at the
   live-modification station on demo day.

## 19. Biggest implementation risks

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **MLX90614 cannot see through plastic.** Acrylic and most plastics are opaque in the 8–14 µm band it uses. A sealed clear window **blinds the cloud sensor.** | **Project-threatening** | Open aperture under a rain hood, tilted ~15° for drainage; **or** a thin LDPE film window (polyethylene is reasonably LWIR-transparent — a bag or cling film, calibrated in place, replaced periodically). Test this in **week 6**, not week 12. |
| **MLX90614 I2C is finicky on the Pi** (SMBus / repeated-start behaviour) | High | Budget real time. Common fixes: lower the bus baudrate (`dtparam=i2c_arm_baudrate=50000`), or use the `i2c-gpio` bitbang overlay on separate pins. Get it reading in week 6 or reconsider the sensor. |
| **Weather refuses to cooperate.** Too few clear nights for a meaningful matrix | High | Log from week 6. Observation-level not night-level labels. Provoked conditions + replay harness. Narrow the claim (§14). |
| **TSL2591 at the bottom of its range.** Night sky is near its noise floor | Medium | Long integration times, dark-frame/offset characterisation in a sealed box, report *relative* brightness unless the SQM calibration happens. |
| **Humidity correction may not separate cleanly** | Medium | If regression on your own data fails to separate humid-clear from overcast, say so and narrow the cloud claim to dry conditions. That is a legitimate result. |

I've read CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, the three docs, the handout's M3 row, and all of `src/` and `tests/`. Here's the plan. I haven't written any code yet.

# M3 plan: sensors → rings → fusiond → stored, supervised by dskyd

## What I found that the plan has to account for

1. **One blocker in Nick's record header.** `record-and-ipc.md` says START (kind 6) and the `source_id`s 1–6 were confirmed on 2026-10-28, but `src/common/record.h` doesn't define them. The sequence check can't tell a restart from a loss without START records. Question 1 at the bottom.
2. **`stored` doesn't exist.** `origin/main` has nothing newer than `b8a0fae`. Nick's store library has open/append/close only: no recovery, no fsync, one file. So I'll write the thin daemon you described and stop there.
3. **"SIMULATED flag":** the record format already has `DSM_FLAG_SYNTHETIC` ("all replayed or provoked data"). I'll set that bit rather than add a new one, so Nick's format doesn't change.
4. **MLX90614 PEC has never been checked on hardware.** Nick's §1 reads used `i2cget` without PEC. If the Pi's clock-stretching problem corrupts reads, every PEC check fails, cloudd exits "absent" after 3 reads, and dskyd parks it as DEAD. That would be a hardware finding, not a bug in our code. So the runbook starts with one-shot probes (`cloudd --once`), and the log line `pec_mismatch` tells you exactly what happened.
5. **topeka has `/dev/i2c-0..12`.** Those are the workstation's own buses. I'll only compile the i2c-dev backend here and never run it, so its first real execution is Nick's run.
6. **`/dev/shm` is shared by every user on topeka.** Shared-memory names include the uid and a per-run tag (`/dsky-<uid>-<tag>-sky`).
7. **Mac limits:** macOS has no `sem_timedwait`, no process-shared unnamed semaphores, and no AF_UNIX `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. The libraries and `make test` stay portable. The semaphore wait falls back to a 100 ms poll on Mac. The daemons are built and run on Linux only. I can't test the Mac build myself, so Nick runs `make test` on his Mac once.

## Files

| Path | Owner | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `src/ipc/log.{c,h}` | Liam | `<ISO time> <mono s> proc[pid] LEVEL event k=v`. Every line from a sim build ends in `data=SIMULATED` |
| `src/ipc/ring.{c,h}` | Liam | SPSC shared-memory ring + wakeup semaphore |
| `src/ipc/seqpkt.{c,h}` | Liam | SEQPACKET client: non-blocking send, reconnect. Used by fusiond and dskyd |
| `src/ipc/proto.h` | Liam | Exit codes, naming of shm and socket paths, child argv conventions |
| `src/sensors/i2c.h` | Liam | The backend interface |
| `src/sensors/i2c_dev.c` | Liam | **Linux only.** `ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` on `/dev/i2c-1` |
| `src/sensors/i2c_sim.c` | Liam | Seeded chip models of the TSL2591 and MLX90614 registers, plus fault injection |
| `src/sensors/tsl2591.{c,h}`, `mlx90614.{c,h}` | Liam | Chip drivers: probe, read, and pure conversion functions |
| `src/sensors/sensord.{c,h}`, `skyd.c`, `cloudd.c` | Liam | Shared sample loop; the two daemon mains |
| `src/super/policy.{c,h}` | Liam | Pure restart policy: backoff, storm, DEAD, hang. Time is passed in, so it's unit-testable |
| `src/super/procstat.{c,h}`, `dskyd.c` | Liam | `/proc` RSS and CPU; the supervisor |
| `src/fusion/fusiond.c` | Liam | Drains the rings and forwards records. No analysis yet |
| `src/store/stored.c` | **Nick** (thin) | Accepts the socket and calls `store_append`. Header: "owner: Nick; batching, fsync policy and recovery are his to implement" |
| `tools/dsmdump.c` | both | Prints records. `--check` verifies CRC, slot alignment, and per-(source, run) seq gaps and duplicates |
| `tools/run-m3.sh`, `tools/sim-faults.sh`, `docs/m3-runbook.md` | Liam | Nick's run script, the fault script run on topeka, and Nick's instructions |

## Interfaces (abridged)

```c
/* sensors/i2c.h: one implementation is linked per binary, chosen at build time */
int  i2c_open(const char *dev, struct i2c_bus **out);                 /* 0 or -errno */
int  i2c_write(struct i2c_bus *, uint8_t addr, const uint8_t *w, size_t wn);
int  i2c_write_read(struct i2c_bus *, uint8_t addr,                   /* one I2C_RDWR: */
                    const uint8_t *w, size_t wn, uint8_t *r, size_t rn); /* repeated start */
void i2c_close(struct i2c_bus *);
extern const bool i2c_simulated;      /* sim: sets SYNTHETIC on every record */

/* ipc/ring.h: head and tail are free-running uint32; _Static_assert(ATOMIC_INT_LOCK_FREE == 2) */
int  ring_create(const char *name, uint32_t nslots, struct ring **); /* dskyd: reattach if header valid */
int  ring_attach(const char *name, struct ring **);
bool ring_push(struct ring *, const struct dsm_record *sealed); /* copy, then release-store head; full → overrun++, false */
int  ring_peek(struct ring *, struct dsm_record *out);          /* acquire head; copy out; RING_TORN if CRC fails */
void ring_advance(struct ring *);                               /* release-store tail, only after forwarding */
void ring_wake(struct ring *); int ring_wait(struct ring *, int timeout_ms);
```

- **Sim backend.** It emulates the chips at the register level, so on topeka the real driver code runs: the TSL2591 ID/STATUS/data registers, and MLX90614 reads with a correct PEC. Faults are control files in `$DSKY_SIM_DIR`:
  - `<chip>.unplug`: every transfer fails with `EREMOTEIO`, and the sensor stays unplugged across restarts.
  - `<chip>.hang`: the transfer blocks.
  - `<chip>.readerr` (contains N): the next N transfers fail with `EIO`.
  - `mlx90614.badpec` (contains N): the next N reads come back with a wrong PEC.
- **`pipeline` and `sim` are separate builds** (`build/pipeline/`, `build/sim/`). A pipeline binary has no sim code linked in, so it can't produce simulated data by accident, and a grader can confirm that in a minute.
- **TSL2591, every 5 s:** read STATUS (AVALID) and the 4 data bytes in one transfer, 2 transfers per sample as DESIGN says. Integration is fixed at 600 ms. The gain auto-ranges between samples; a gain change rewrites CONTROL and toggles AEN. A saturated reading becomes a SAMPLE without `VALID`. Payload as in the doc: CH0, CH1, gain ×, ms.
- **MLX90614, every 1 s:** read Ta (0x06) and Tobj1 (0x07) with PEC. A PEC mismatch counts as a failed read. Error bit 15 set → SAMPLE without `VALID`. Values in m°C: `raw×20−273150`.
- **Datasheet facts:** I'll fetch both datasheets and cite the section in comments. Every value that affects hardware behavior gets the comment `assumed, verify on darksky.local`. I won't invent a TSL2591 worked example; if the datasheet has none, the test says so.
- **Records and exit codes.**
  - Each run starts with START (seq 0, `v[0]` = run number from dskyd's argv).
  - First failed read → FAULT. 3 consecutive failures → FAULT, then exit 3 (`EXIT_ABSENT`).
  - Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 sensor absent.
- **Liveness.** fd 3 is the write end of the pipe, set non-blocking. Sensors write one byte per loop iteration; fusiond and stored write one per 1 s poll.
- **dskyd.**
  - Creates the rings before forking. Starts stored first, then fusiond, then the sensors.
  - Main loop: `poll()` over the liveness pipes plus a self-pipe for SIGCHLD, then a `waitpid(WNOHANG)` loop.
  - 20 s without a liveness byte → SIGKILL. Crash backoff 1→60 s, reset after 60 s healthy. 5 crashes in 300 s → DEAD. Exit 3 → DEAD with a 60 s re-probe.
  - Pipes and the socket are close-on-exec. Children set `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` (Linux).
  - HEARTBEAT 10 s after each child starts, then hourly.
  - SIGTERM: stops the sensors, then fusiond (which drains the rings first), then stored, with 5 s each before SIGKILL. Then it unlinks the shm and the socket.
- **fusiond.** If stored is down, it stops draining and the rings act as the buffer. The 4096-record buffer in the design is for fusiond's own FEATURE/STATE records, which don't exist yet, so it's deferred.

## Commits (tests first in each, real output shown, then I pause)

0. *(only if you choose option A in question 1)* `M3: START kind and source ids in record.h`
1. `M3: structured log library` (shared by all daemons)
2. `M3: shared-memory SPSC ring`. Tests:
   - Basic use, full ring (drop the new record, count the overrun), wraparound near `UINT32_MAX`, reattach.
   - **Forked producer SIGKILLed mid-stream:** a test hook makes the slot copy byte-by-byte and slow, so a kill lands mid-copy. The test asserts 0 torn records and a gapless seq across restarts.
   - **Negative control:** the test itself publishes first and copies second, and asserts that the torn record *is* detected. This shows the test can catch a broken ring.
3. `M3: I2C backend interface and seeded sim backend with faults`
4. `M3: TSL2591 driver and conversions`
5. `M3: MLX90614 driver, PEC, conversions` (datasheet SMBus read-word example as a test)
6. `M3: i2c-dev backend and Linux-only Makefile split` (compiled on topeka only, never run here)
7. `M3: supervisor restart policy` (pure functions, fake clock)
8. `M3: skyd and cloudd daemons` (plus `--once` probe mode)
9. `M3: thin stored over the store API` (Nick's area, kept thin)
10. `M3: dsmdump record dump and sequence checker`
11. `M3: fusiond ring drain to stored`
12. `M3: dskyd supervisor`
13. `M3: make pipeline / make sim with end-to-end seq check`. `make sim SAN=1` runs the chain under ASan. The Makefile also gets a fix for its known bug: ASan builds go to `build/asan/`, so `make memcheck` stops picking up the ASan binary.
14. `M3: sim fault script`. Covers kill -9, hang, storm, unplug and re-probe, SIGTERM exit codes, and fd counts in `/proc/<pid>/fd` before and after restarts. About 4 minutes, run by `make simfaults`.
15. `M3: run-m3.sh and Nick's runbook`. The log is saved to `evidence/m3-<host>-<timestamp>.log`; the data directory is gitignored.
16. `M3: progress log, CLAUDE.md ownership (src/ipc, src/fusion)`
17. *(only if everything else is done, and only after I ask you)* envd

I'll ask before pushing.

**Not done in M3, and stated in the runbook:**

# M3 notes for Nick (from Liam's planning session, 2026-10-28)

These came from reading the repo at `b8a0fae` against `DESIGN.md` and `docs/record-and-ipc.md`.
No code was written. Each item is something the M3 code will run into.

## 1. `record.h` is missing START and the source ids

`record-and-ipc.md` lists these as confirmed on 2026-10-28, but `src/common/record.h` doesn't
define them:

- `DSM_KIND_START = 6`. Without START, a sequence check can't tell a restart from lost data:
  `seq` counts per (source, run), and START is what opens a run.
- The `source_id`s: 1 `skyd`, 2 `cloudd`, 3 `envd`, 4 `fusiond`, 5 `dskyd`, 6 `stored`
  (0 reserved).
- Also missing: `DSM_FLAG_CLOCK_UNSYNC` = bit 4. It's still marked *proposed*, so it can wait.

All three are additive enum values; the layout doesn't change.

## 2. `stored` doesn't exist yet

`src/store/` has the library only: `store_open`, `store_append`, `store_close`, one file, no
daemon. The library still has no recovery (a torn tail means the next append lands out of
line), no `fsync` and no write batching. Until recovery exists, killing `stored` mid-write can
leave the file misaligned. Also, a `SOCK_SEQPACKET` `send()` that succeeds doesn't mean `stored`
appended the record: without an ack, a `kill -9` of `stored` can lose whatever is in its
socket buffer.

## 3. Simulated data: use `DSM_FLAG_SYNTHETIC`

The flag already exists (bit 2, "all replayed or provoked data"). A sim backend should set it on
every record, so no new flag is needed. Log lines from sim runs need their own label too
(CLAUDE.md: "labeled as such everywhere it appears").

## 4. MLX90614 PEC has never been checked on hardware

The hardware-log §1 reads were `i2cget` SMBus read-word without the PEC byte. PEC is CRC-8
(poly `0x07`) over addr+W, command, addr+R, LSB, MSB. The read needs a repeated start: one
`ioctl(I2C_RDWR)` with a 1-byte write message and a 3-byte read message. If the Pi's I2C
clock-stretching problem corrupts reads, every PEC check fails. A daemon that treats 3 failed
reads as "sensor absent" would then park `cloudd` as DEAD, and that looks like a software bug
when it isn't one.

**Suggestion:** before running the full pipeline, run a one-shot probe (e.g. `cloudd --once`)
that reads Ta and Tobj with the PEC checked and prints the raw bytes and the computed PEC. If it
fails, the fixes already noted in hardware-log "Problems encountered" apply: lower
`i2c_arm_baudrate`, or use `i2c-gpio`. Paste that output before changing any code.

## 5. macOS can't run the IPC as designed

Taken from documentation; not yet tried on a Mac:

- no `sem_timedwait`
- no process-shared unnamed semaphores (`sem_init(pshared=1)` fails)
- no `AF_UNIX` `SOCK_SEQPACKET`

So the daemons and the ring's semaphore wakeup are Linux-only. To keep `make test` working on
the Mac, keep the libraries portable: either guard the wakeup with `#ifdef` (with a short-poll
fallback on macOS), or keep it out of `test_all`. `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` and `/proc/<pid>/stat*` are
Linux-only too.

## 6. Makefile: `make memcheck` after `make asan` runs valgrind on the ASan binary

`asan` and `all` both build `build/test_all`. After `make asan`, `memcheck`'s prerequisite
`all` is already up to date, so valgrind runs the ASan-instrumented binary and crashes.
Workaround today: `make clean` first. Fix: build the ASan binary to its own path, e.g.
`build/asan/test_all`, so the two targets never share an output. `vgcore.*` also belongs in
`.gitignore`.

## Side notes

- On CS department machines, `/dev/shm` is shared by every user, so shm names need the uid or a
  per-run tag in them.
- Those machines also have their own `/dev/i2c-*` buses. Never run the i2c-dev backend there.

1	# M3 plan: both sensors through the real pipeline into real storage
2	
3	Agreed by Nick and Liam on a call, 2026-10-28. **Canvas (TP-D2) closes Fri 2026-10-30, 8 pm MT.**
4	Progress against this plan goes in [`progress-log.md`](progress-log.md), newest entry first.
5	
6	## What M3 requires
7	
8	Spec §6, and row 2 of the Canvas TP-D2 rubric: *"Checkpoint demo: both sensors flowing through the
9	real pipeline into real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out."*
10	
11	## Decisions
12	
13	- **M3 slice: sensor programs → `stored` → store file**, over `AF_UNIX` `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. The
14	  shared-memory rings, `fusiond` and `dskyd` come at M4. `DESIGN.md`'s architecture is unchanged;
15	  M3 builds its two ends and connects them directly.
16	- **`SOCK_SEQPACKET`, as designed. It runs on Linux only:** on macOS `socket()` fails with
17	  "Protocol not supported" (checked 2026-10-28). So `stored`, its client and their tests build and
18	  run only on Linux (the Pi, the CS machines). The portable code (record, CRC, logger, store
19	  library, conversion math, `dsq`) still builds and tests on a Mac.
20	- **Mechanism shown working at M3: D** (crash recovery + `fsync`). E comes at M4.
21	- **"Both sensors" = TSL2591 (`skyd`) + MLX90614 (`cloudd`).** `envd` (BME280) as well if time.
22	- **Runtime files live outside the deployed tree**, so `make deploy` never touches them:
23	  `~/dsm/data/seg-000001.dsm` and `~/dsm/run/stored.sock`. One segment for M3; rotation is M4.
24	
25	## Who does what (no file is edited by both)
26	
27	| Area | Files | Who |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| Done: CRC, record, store writer, **crash recovery** (`bc6d3bc`) | `src/common/crc32.*`, `src/common/record.*`, `src/store/store.*` | Nick |
30	| **Shared pieces**, written first (2026-10-28 evening), then changed only by agreement | `src/common/record.h` additions, `src/common/log.{c,h}`, `src/store/store_client.h` | Nick |
31	| **Storage side** (S1–S6 below) | `src/store/` (`store.c` additions, `stored.c`, `store_client.c`), `src/dsq/`, `tests/test_store.c`, `tests/test_dsq.c`, `tests/itest_stored.c` | Liam |
32	| **Sensor side** (N1–N4 below) | `src/sensors/` (conversion math, I2C layer, `sensorcheck`, `skyd`, `cloudd`, `envd`), `tests/test_convert.c`, `tools/run-m3.sh` | Nick |
33	| **Integration + the D demo** on `darksky.local`, the only wired kit | `docs/m3-checkpoint.md` | Nick runs it, with Liam's pushed code |
34	
35	Files both of you touch: the `Makefile` (each edits **only their own section**), `tests/suites.h`
36	and `tests/test_main.c` (one line each per new suite), `docs/progress-log.md`. Rule: `git pull
37	--rebase` before every commit, small commits, never reformat the other side's lines.
38	
39	## The contract between the two halves
40	
41	### The socket
42	
43	- `AF_UNIX`, `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. Path given on `stored`'s command line.
44	- **One message = one sealed `struct dsm_record`, exactly 48 bytes.** Nothing else is ever sent.
45	- Clients only send. `stored` never replies.
46	- Many clients at once: one per sensor program now, `fusiond` and `dskyd` at M4.
47	- `stored` is the only process that writes the data file, and the only one that ever truncates it.
48	- Why SEQPACKET rather than a stream: message boundaries are kept, so one bad message never
49	  misaligns the ones after it, and the connection can stay open.
50	
51	### The client API: `src/store/store_client.h`
52	
53	Nick writes this header with the shared pieces. Liam implements `src/store/store_client.c`.
54	
55	```c
56	struct store_client;
57	
58	/* Remembers the socket path. Does not connect yet, so it works whether
59	 * or not stored is running. NULL only if out of memory or the path is
60	 * too long for a sockaddr_un (errno says which). */
61	struct store_client *store_client_new(const char *socket_path);
62	
63	/* Sends one sealed record as one message. Never blocks: if stored is

Agreed by Nick and Liam on a call, 2026-10-28. **Canvas (TP-D2) closes Fri 2026-10-30, 8 pm MT.**
Progress against this plan goes in [`progress-log.md`](progress-log.md), newest entry first.

## What M3 requires

Spec §6, and row 2 of the Canvas TP-D2 rubric: *"Checkpoint demo: both sensors flowing through the
real pipeline into real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out."*

## Decisions

- **M3 slice: sensor programs → `stored` → store file**, over `AF_UNIX` `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. The
  shared-memory rings, `fusiond` and `dskyd` come at M4. `DESIGN.md`'s architecture is unchanged;
  M3 builds its two ends and connects them directly.
- **`SOCK_SEQPACKET`, as designed. It runs on Linux only:** on macOS `socket()` fails with
  "Protocol not supported" (checked 2026-10-28). So `stored`, its client and their tests build and
  run only on Linux (the Pi, the CS machines). The portable code (record, CRC, logger, store
  library, conversion math, `dsq`) still builds and tests on a Mac.
- **Mechanism shown working at M3: D** (crash recovery + `fsync`). E comes at M4.
- **"Both sensors" = TSL2591 (`skyd`) + MLX90614 (`cloudd`).** `envd` (BME280) as well if time.
- **Runtime files live outside the deployed tree**, so `make deploy` never touches them:
  `~/dsm/data/seg-000001.dsm` and `~/dsm/run/stored.sock`. One segment for M3; rotation is M4.

## Who does what (no file is edited by both)

| Area | Files | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Done: CRC, record, store writer, **crash recovery** (`bc6d3bc`) | `src/common/crc32.*`, `src/common/record.*`, `src/store/store.*` | Nick |
| **Shared pieces**, written first (2026-10-28 evening), then changed only by agreement | `src/common/record.h` additions, `src/common/log.{c,h}`, `src/store/store_client.h` | Nick |

struct store_client;

+#ifndef DSM_STORE_CLIENT_H
+#define DSM_STORE_CLIENT_H
+
+#include "common/record.h"
+
+#include <stdint.h>
+
+/* The sending half of the stored protocol, used by every process that
+ * produces records (the sensor programs now; fusiond and dskyd at M4).
+ *
+ * The protocol (docs/m3-plan.md): AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET, one sealed
+ * 48-byte struct dsm_record per message, clients only send, stored never
+ * replies. Linux only: macOS does not support SOCK_SEQPACKET.
+ *
+ * This header is the agreement between the sensor side and the storage
+ * side. Change it only when both partners agree. */
+
+/* Opaque: only store_client.c can see inside. */
+struct store_client;
+
+/* Remembers the socket path. Does not connect yet, so it works whether
+ * or not stored is running. NULL only if out of memory or the path is
+ * too long for a sockaddr_un (errno says which). */
+struct store_client *store_client_new(const char *socket_path);
+
+/* Sends one sealed record as one message. Never blocks: if stored is
+ * down, slow or gone, the record is dropped and counted, and the caller
+ * keeps sampling (the seq gap shows the loss). Reconnects on its own,
+ * at most one attempt per second. Returns 0 if sent, -1 if dropped. */
+int store_client_send(struct store_client *c, const struct dsm_record *r);
+
+/* Records dropped since store_client_new(). */
+uint64_t store_client_dropped(const struct store_client *c);
+
+/* Closes the connection and frees. NULL-safe. */
+void store_client_free(struct store_client *c);
+
+#endif
